DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 9.0.23-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v9.0.124 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v9.0.124), and its assemblies record that tag's commit, f4699d9. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships ASP.NET Core 9 at its own .NET version in three places: the shared framework in aspnetcore9-runtime, the shared framework in the .NET SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap, and the ASP.NET Core runtime pack NuGet package that dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap also holds: 9.0.12 through 9.0.22 in the earlier builds and 9.0.23 in both 9.0.23-r0 builds, and each of those copies contains Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.dll. The reference assemblies of the same name in aspnetcore9-targeting-pack, dotnet9-runtime-artifacts and the SDK's targeting pack are compile-time metadata with no implementation code. The range ends at 9.0.23-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-114146 (GHSA-67wp-ghc2-fw2g) is an ASP.NET Core elevation of privilege: SignalR connections are not consistently bound to the identity negotiated when the connection was established, so injected messages can run Hub invocations as the victim. Microsoft lists the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime 10.0 packages up to 10.0.14 as affected and fixed it in ASP.NET Core 10.0.15 (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-67wp-ghc2-fw2g, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/504), and the .NET 10.0.15 release notes ship SDK 10.0.404 with the 10.0.15 runtimes (https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.15/10.0.15.md). DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. Inspected every published dotnet-sdk-10 package for amd64 and arm64 (10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1), including the .nupkg and .zip archives bundled in them: each holds one .NET runtime under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version> and one ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, at the same version, and the dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages from the same source hold only a configuration file and its changelog. 10.0.301-0 holds 10.0.9, 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1 hold 10.0.10, 10.0.400-1 holds 10.0.11, 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1 hold 10.0.12, 10.0.402-0 holds 10.0.13, 10.0.403-0 holds 10.0.14, and 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1 hold 10.0.15. In 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1 on both architectures, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.dll in the shared framework contains UserIdentitySnapshot, the type Microsoft's fix adds to record the negotiated identity (commit https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/ea1597f12b56b32769db8fffc1a80f4186e73922 on the dotnet/dotnet release/10.0.1xx branch, first included in the v10.0.115 tag); the copy in every earlier build lacks it. The shared framework assemblies also record the dotnet/dotnet commit they were built from: those holding 10.0.9 through 10.0.14 were built from the v10.0.109 through v10.0.114 tags, which do not contain the fix commit, and those holding 10.0.15 from the v10.0.115 tag, which does. The only other copies of the SignalR and Http.Connections assemblies in each build are the reference assemblies under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref, and none sits inside the bundled archives. The range ends at 10.0.404-0, the first published build with the fix.

Inspected every published dotnet-sdk-9 package for amd64 and arm64 (9.0.315-0, 9.0.316-0, 9.0.316-1, 9.0.317-1, 9.0.318-0, 9.0.318-1, 9.0.319-0, 9.0.320-0, 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1), checksums verified against the repository index, including the .nupkg and .zip archives bundled in them: each holds one .NET runtime under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version> and one ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, at the same version, and the dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config packages from the same source hold only a configuration file and its changelog. 9.0.315-0 holds 9.0.17, 9.0.316-0 and 9.0.316-1 hold 9.0.18, 9.0.317-1 holds 9.0.19, 9.0.318-0 and 9.0.318-1 hold 9.0.20, 9.0.319-0 holds 9.0.21, 9.0.320-0 holds 9.0.22, and 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1 hold 9.0.23; the shared-framework assemblies of each build carry, in their informational version, the dotnet/aspnetcore commit of the matching v9.0.N release tag. In 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1 on both architectures, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.dll in the shared framework contains UserIdentitySnapshot; the copy in every earlier build lacks it. The only other Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections.dll in each build is the reference assembly under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref, and none sits inside the bundled archives. The range ends at 9.0.321-0, the first published build with the fix.
